preamble: The shift from a retroflex stop [ʈ] to an alveolar stop [t] is a form of de-retroflexion involving apical displacement—moving from postvocalic to prevocalic position while fronting from the hard palate to the alveolar ridge. This process is well-documented in South Dravidian languages (Telugu, Kannada) where Proto-Dravidian retroflex stops underwent systematic repositioning and deretroflexion. Ostapirat's Proto-Kra retroflex stops likewise appear as alveolar [t] in Buyang and Laha.

examples.note: Major apical displacement: retroflex stops shifted from postvocalic to prevocalic position, often deretroflexing to alveolar [t] or voiced [d]. Proto-Dravidian *uẓ-u 'plow' → Telugu ḍu-kki; *car-a-cu → Telugu trācu.
Kannada merged the three-way coronal distinction into two-way dental-retroflex, with many retroflex stops dentalizing to [t].

examples.to: Buyang (Langjia) ma⁰ ta⁵⁴, Laha (Noong Lay) ta³
examples.note: Ostapirat's (2000) Proto-Kra retroflex stop; Miyake (2021) instead reconstructs disyllabic *mata for this etymon, so the retroflex series itself is contested.

examples.to: Buyang (Langjia) qa⁰ tu⁵⁴, En (Nung Ven) tu⁵⁴

examples.note: A'ou Gelao instead shows spirantized reflexes (Hongfeng ɕaŋ⁴²).
